on_h_iguana_wall.blurb: A steep wall on the Niagara Escarpment at Mount Nemo, tucked just under the main lookout above Burlington. The name comes from a clifftop boulder shaped like a lizard. Nearly all of the 19 climbs are bolted sport lines, with three trad routes mixed in. The grades sit mostly in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with 5.10 the most common and only a couple of easy or moderate lines, so it suits climbers who already lead steady 5.10. To get to the base, walk the lookout trail, then drop down one of the gullies on either side of the wall and loop back along the foot of the cliff.

on_roadside.blurb: An ice and mixed crag on the north side of Papineau Lake in the Madawaska Valley of eastern Ontario, close to the road. Two large cliffs hold bolted mixed lines and some pure ice, with boulders at the base of the bigger one. Of the 19 climbs, most are mixed, running from around M4 up to M8 with the bulk in the M5 to M7 range, and a handful of ice routes sit at WI3 and WI4. The lines are straightforward and fun rather than serious, which makes it a handy place to learn tool technique or work through steady mixed grades in winter.

on_echo_crag.blurb: A granite crag just outside Lively, west of Sudbury, on a short trail through the woods. The West and Main walls hold about twenty routes, nearly all bolted, so most of the 19 climbs here are sport with a few trad lines. It is not a beginner spot: grades start around 5.9 and the majority fall at 5.12, with several 5.10s and 5.11s as stepping stones. Anchors are easy to reach from the top, which makes the crag popular for top-roping as well as leading. Expect a quiet, bush setting rather than a roadside cliff.
on_echo_crag.approach: About 1.5 km on a trail heading west into the woods from the highway.

on_granary_lake.blurb: A winter waterfall ice venue in southern Algoma, north of Blind River, where tall cliffs rise from the north shore of the lake. The 18 ice routes cover a wide range, from short easy flows through a solid core of WI3, up to a few steep WI4 and WI5 lines. Climbs reach roughly 45 metres, and the steep curtains are the highlight. The walk in is short, crossing the frozen lake. Because it offers plenty of moderate ice alongside harder objectives, it works for mixed-ability groups, though you should expect cold lakeside conditions.

on_malen_s_wall.blurb: A newer wall within Metcalfe Rock in the Beaver Valley area, sitting beside the Boiler Plate Wall. It has 19 climbs, a mix of 11 bolted lines and 8 trad routes, with some chimney and arete features. Difficulty is broad: a few easy lines near the bottom of the scale, a solid group of moderates around 5.7 to 5.8, then a cluster of 5.10s and a few harder pitches up to 5.12. That blend suits newer leaders working up the grades as well as strong climbers. The wall catches sun in the afternoon, while the surrounding crag tends to be shady and treed.
